era: Root Shock: War Ignites a Global Energy Crisis (Feb–Jun 2026)

events.title: War Begins — Hormuz Shipping Grinds to a Halt
events.detail: The US-Israel decapitation strikes on Iran (Feb 28, 2026) trigger immediate Iranian threats to close the Strait of Hormuz. Tanker traffic falls roughly 70% within days as the IRGC issues warnings against transit; war-risk insurance premiums surge fivefold within 48 hours as major marine insurers pull coverage or reprice it at roughly 60x pre-crisis rates.

events.title: Brent Crude Tops $100 for the First Time Since 2022
events.detail: Brent crude surpasses $100 a barrel on March 8, 2026, the first time since the immediate aftermath of Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Analysts cite the near-total halt of Hormuz tanker traffic — the strait normally carries about one-fifth of global oil supply and 20% of global LNG — as the driver.

events.title: IEA Approves Record 400-Million-Barrel Emergency Release
events.detail: The International Energy Agency triggers the largest coordinated emergency oil stock release in its history — up to 400 million barrels from member reserves — in response to the Hormuz shock (announced around March 11). The US, Japan, South Korea and China join; India releases 5 million barrels from its own strategic reserve, which at the time held barely 9–10 days of cover versus the IEA's 90-day benchmark.

events.title: Iranian Strike on Qatar's Ras Laffan Cuts LNG Capacity 17%
events.detail: Iran strikes Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG complex on March 18, 2026, reducing liquefaction capacity by roughly 17% with repair timelines estimated at three to five years. Asian LNG spot prices jump more than 140% in the aftermath, compounding the crude oil shock for import-dependent economies.

events.title: Egypt Raises Fuel Prices 14–17% as Subsidy Bill Balloons
events.detail: Egypt raises domestic fuel prices 14–17% in March 2026 as rising global energy costs strain its subsidized bread and fuel programs. The move follows warnings that Cairo's cereal-import and fiscal-subsidy exposure make it one of the Arab world's most vulnerable economies to the Hormuz shock.

events.title: Sri Lanka Reimposes QR-Code Fuel Rationing
events.detail: Sri Lanka, which imports roughly 60% of its energy needs, reintroduces a QR-code fuel rationing system (motorbikes 8L, three-wheelers 20L, cars 25L, buses 100L, lorries 200L). Officials warn that if oil prices hold near $120/bbl, the annual fuel import bill could reach $4.5–$5 billion, risking a fresh balance-of-payments crisis just years after the country's 2022 default.

events.title: Brent Peaks Near $118 in Largest-Ever Monthly Oil Price Rise
events.detail: Brent crude closes March 2026 at roughly $118.35/bbl — an increase of about 65% ($46/bbl) on the month, the largest monthly rise on record, with intraday spikes reported as high as $126. The IEA characterizes the disruption as "the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market."

events.title: IMF: 'No Painless Exit' From the War's Energy Shock
events.detail: At the IMF-World Bank Spring Meetings (April 9), Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warns there is no painless exit from the Hormuz-driven energy shock. The IMF's baseline scenario (a short-lived conflict, 19% energy-price rise) projects 3.1% global growth and 4.4% inflation for 2026; an adverse scenario puts growth at 2.5% with 5.4% inflation, and a severe scenario at 2% growth with 5.8% inflation.

events.title: Ceasefire Fails to Revive Hormuz Shipping — 20,000 Mariners Stranded
events.detail: Despite the April 8 US-Iran ceasefire, tanker traffic through Hormuz remains far below pre-war levels. The IMO reports on April 21 that roughly 20,000 mariners and 2,000 ships remain stranded in the Persian Gulf, underscoring that a political truce has not restored normal maritime insurance or transit conditions.

events.title: OPEC: Hormuz Closure Cuts Cartel Output 30%, Locks Away Spare Capacity
events.detail: OPEC reports on May 13 that the Hormuz closure has cut the cartel's oil production by roughly 30%. Saudi Arabia and the UAE, which hold virtually all of OPEC's meaningful spare capacity (near 10 million bpd by April), are themselves geographically dependent on the strait — leaving the shock absorber that markets need most largely inaccessible even as Riyadh reroutes 60–70% of exports via a 1981 Red Sea pipeline.

events.title: Islamabad MOU Signed — Oil Markets Rally on Reopening Hopes
events.detail: The US, Israel and Iran sign the 14-point Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding on June 17, 2026. Oil and shipping markets rally on hopes of a durable Hormuz reopening; OPEC Secretary General Haitham al-Ghais tells CNBC on June 18 that the last four months have proven "just how critical that waterway is" for global energy markets.

events.title: Oil Prices Fall as Tankers Begin Exiting the Strait
events.detail: By late June, oil prices ease as ship-tracking data shows tankers cautiously resuming Hormuz transits under the MOU framework. The relief proves short-lived: Iran briefly re-closes the strait on June 20 citing alleged Israeli ceasefire violations, before transits resume again days later.

events.title: MOU Collapse Sends Oil Back Above $90 Amid Fresh Tanker Strikes
events.detail: After Iranian strikes on four commercial vessels in the strait (July 6–7), Trump declares the Islamabad MOU "over" on July 8 and the US resumes strikes and a naval blockade. Energy markets reprice the reopening risk premium overnight; Brent, which had dipped toward $71.57 on July 1, rebounds sharply through the month.

events.title: FAO Food Price Index Hits Three-Year High
events.detail: The FAO Food Price Index climbs to 131.1 in July 2026, its highest level in three years, as Black Sea and Hormuz disruptions push global wheat prices up 5.8% and vegetable oils to a four-year peak. FAO Chief Economist Máximo Torero warns that the wars in Iran and Ukraine, combined with El Niño weather effects, create "a perfect storm" that will push food prices higher still into 2027.

events.title: WFP: Global Hunger Could Reach Record Levels
events.detail: The World Food Programme warns that the virtual shipping standstill in Hormuz and mounting Red Sea risk are deepening hunger well beyond the Middle East, with 45 million people at risk of acute hunger directly tied to the conflict. WFP projects a 21% rise in extreme hunger for West and Central Africa, 17% for East and Southern Africa, and 24% for Asia — against a backdrop of severe WFP funding shortfalls.

events.title: FAO: Fertilizer Shock Threatens 2026–27 Harvests
events.detail: A joint FAO/regional food-security assessment finds that 20–45% of key agrifood inputs — chiefly urea and ammonia fertilizer, of which the Gulf supplies 30–35% of global exports — depend on Hormuz passage. Nitrogen fertilizer costs have roughly doubled versus 2024 levels, with farmers in several countries shifting to less fertilizer-intensive crops ahead of the next planting cycle.

events.title: Suez Canal Traffic Remains 57% Below Pre-Crisis Levels
events.detail: Combined Red Sea Houthi risk and the Hormuz war keep Suez Canal transits roughly 57–60% below pre-diversion levels through mid-2026, with Cape of Good Hope volumes hitting a record 24 million deadweight tonnes by late April. Major liners including CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd continue routing the bulk of Asia-Europe trade around Africa, adding 10–14 days and materially higher fuel and charter costs per voyage.

events.title: Lawmakers Scrutinize Corporate Price Gouging Amid Fuel Spike
events.detail: US lawmakers press the FTC over concerns that companies are widening profit margins under cover of the war rather than passing through actual input-cost increases, as US gasoline prices jump roughly $1.16/gallon and diesel and jet fuel post even sharper gains. The debate mirrors similar accusations leveled at fuel retailers and shippers in Asia and Europe.

era: August Standoff: Prices Climb, No Resolution in Sight

events.title: Iran Advances Bill to Bar US- and Israeli-Linked Vessels
events.detail: Iran's parliament advances a bill on August 6, 2026 to formally bar vessels linked to the US and Israel from the strait, hardening the legal basis for continued restrictions even as diplomatic contacts with Oman continue.

events.title: Iran and Oman Reach Shipping-Corridor Framework — Full Reopening Still Withheld
events.detail: Iran and Oman reach a shipping-corridor framework on August 7–8 that stops short of a full reopening. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Iran and Oman are close to agreement on Hormuz, but the waterway will not fully reopen until Washington eases sanctions and addresses Iranian demands for war reparations.

events.title: World Bank Cuts 2026 Global Growth Forecast to 2.5%
events.detail: The World Bank lowers its 2026 global growth forecast to 2.5% — down 0.1 point from January and the weakest projection since the pandemic-era outlook of late 2019 — citing the Hormuz-driven energy shock. The Bank warns growth could fall as low as 1.3% if the energy crisis triggers a financial-market shock, and notes the largest downgrades fall on the UAE, Iraq and other Middle Eastern exporters whose export volumes, not just prices, have been hit.

events.title: Deadly Houthi Attack and US Blockade Strike Rattle Oil Markets
events.detail: On August 11, a US Navy helicopter disables the blockade-running cargo ship Vela Nova off Pakistan while Houthi forces kill six people in a 'double-tap' missile strike on the cargo ship Tihamah near Bab al-Mandeb — the first fatal Houthi attack on shipping since the war began. Oil prices rise on the news as hopes for a near-term Hormuz reopening dim further.

events.title: Oil Prices Rise as Attacks Dent Hopes for Strait Reopening
events.detail: Brent crude climbs on August 12 as the Vela Nova and Tihamah incidents compound existing uncertainty over Iran's parliamentary bill and the unfinished Oman framework, pushing traders to price in a longer closure than markets had assumed a week earlier.

events.title: Trump's 'Total Control' Claim Fails to Calm Energy Markets
events.detail: Trump declares on August 12 that the US has 'total control' of the strait and warns Iran could 'get blown away.' Rezaei rejects the claim, saying the strait stays closed until the blockade, sanctions and US regional presence end; Araghchi calls it 'fake intelligence' on August 13. Energy markets treat the claim skeptically — shipping traffic stays near-collapsed at roughly 8 vessels a day versus a 130–140/day pre-war baseline, and Brent holds near $101/bbl rather than falling on the claim.

events.title: War-Risk Insurance Hits 7.5–10% of Hull Value Per Transit
events.detail: War-risk insurance costs for Hormuz transits climb to 7.5–10% of hull value across the tanker segment by August 2026 — a 270,000-DWT crude carrier worth roughly $210 million now pays close to $21 million for a single high-tension transit. Lloyd's of London, which writes 70–80% of the world's marine war-risk business, has layered in higher deductibles and new exclusions as coverage becomes scarcer and more complex.

events.title: FAO Warns Food Prices Will Accelerate Further Into 2027
events.detail: FAO Chief Economist Máximo Torero reiterates through August that the combined effect of the Iran war, Black Sea disruptions and El Niño will push food prices higher still by year-end and into 2027, with reduced global wheat plantings already being reported as farmers economize on fertilizer.

events.title: Egypt Secures $500 Million World Bank Food Security Package
events.detail: Amid mounting fiscal strain from higher import costs, Egypt secures a $500 million World Bank package earmarked to bolster food security and cushion its subsidized bread program against further Hormuz-driven cost shocks.

events.title: India's Decade of Reserve-Building Cushions, but Doesn't Erase, the Shock
events.detail: Analysts credit a decade of Indian strategic reserve expansion and diversified crude sourcing with softening the blow of the Hormuz closure on Asia's third-largest oil importer, even as New Delhi's roughly 21-million-barrel reserve remains far short of the IEA's 90-day benchmark and LPG import costs (60% import-dependent) keep pressuring household budgets.

events.title: EU's Fossil Fuel Import Bill Swells €22 Billion in Six Weeks
events.detail: The European Commission tallies more than €22 billion in additional fossil-fuel import costs over a six-week stretch of the crisis. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen calls for unity and an accelerated pivot to 'homegrown, clean energies,' including a renewed nuclear push, arguing the bloc had made 'a strategic mistake' abandoning reliable low-emissions power.

events.title: OPEC+ Presses Ahead With Monthly Output Increases Despite Closure
events.detail: OPEC+ announces a further monthly output increase in early August, continuing a pattern of symbolic-to-modest production hikes through the closure as members try to signal market confidence even though most of the added barrels cannot physically transit Hormuz, keeping the increases largely notional for global supply.

events.title: Iran and Oman Finalize Temporary Hormuz Shipping Corridor, Strait Still Officially 'Closed'
events.detail: Building on the Aug 7-8 framework talks, Iran and Oman announced a finalized temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz on Aug 26: a roughly 7-mile-wide route with inbound traffic through a northern lane in Iranian waters and outbound traffic through a southern lane in Omani waters, plus a joint mine-clearing project and a revenue-sharing arrangement between the two states. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stressed the corridor is temporary and that the strait remains officially closed pending US sanctions relief under the lapsed June interim deal. Oil prices fell for a third straight day on the news (Brent -2.5% to $86.38/bbl) before steadying near $87-90/bbl on Aug 27 as hot US inflation data offset some of the de-escalation optimism.
